rationale: Both candidates go well beyond the thin ground-truth thread (a few resolved inline comments plus an LGTM) and independently surface the same core themes reviewers cared about — kernel version/pin clarity, Hopper/SM90 gating correctness, and thin test coverage on the masked/piecewise paths — giving comparable recall. X is the more usable review: clearly prioritized, each finding stated once with concrete verified-sounding evidence and a specific fix, and it catches a genuinely novel residual bug (varlen-only impl crashing when only flash_attn_func is required) that mirrors the ground truth's exact concern class. Y's content is comparably grounded (and transparently discloses its PR-time-tree investigation method) but is repetitive — several findings (Blackwell gate, piecewise fallback) are restated three times across sections — and some of its suggested patches are stub placeholders ('...') rather than real fixes, hurting actionability. Neither includes a literal LATENT GAP CHECK section.
